To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclear localization of the Drosophilia circadian clock proteins Period and Timeless is mediated by a nuclear localization signal in Timeless.

a nuclear localization signal in the timeless protein is required for appropriately timing the nuclear accumulation of both the timeless and period proteins in the circadian pacemaker neurons of the brain, and that this signal is necessary for the nuclear accumulation of these proteins in cultured cells.

(1) the nuclear localization signal of Timeless (TIM), a key circadian clock component of Drosophilamelanogaster, is necessary for nuclear localization and function of both TIM and Period (PER); and (2) the TIM nuclear localization signal is required for normal nuclear accumulation of both PER and TIM proteins in pacemaker cells and for normal circadian behavior.

the molecular mechanisms underlying circadian rhythms.
the mechanisms of circadian rhythms.
the mechanisms that control the circadian rhythm, which regulates the daily activities and behaviors of animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nuclear localization signal in the Timeless protein is required for the normal temporal accumulation of Period and Timeless proteins in the nucleus and for the generation and regulation of the circadian rhythms in Drosophila.
a TIM NLS is required for appropriate nuclear accumulation of TIM and PER, and this is an essential part of the mechanism by which circadian rhythms are generated in Drosophila.
a NLS in the Timeless protein is required for appropriate nuclear accumulation of both Period and Timeless proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a NLS in TIM that is necessary for the proper timing of nuclear accumulation of both PER and TIM, and that this NLS is required for the proper functioning of the Drosphila circadian clock.
the TIM NLS is a key temporal delay element in the Drosophilla circadian cycle.
we have found a NLS in the TIM protein that is essential for the circadian clock.

nuclear entry is a key step in the regulation of the circadian clock.
the nuclear accumulation of PER and TIM proteins is a key event in the circadian clock and that the TIM NLS plays a critical role in the regulation of this process.
